newsitem.title: USA: Dry week forecast for Northern Plains and Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Dry week forecast for Northern Plains and Midwest.

text.p: Mostly dry weather was forecast this week for the Midwest and flood-ravaged North Dakota, while widespread showers were likely in dry winter wheat areas of Texas, Oklahoma and southern Kansas, meteorologists said.

"The flood area along the Red River looks like it will be dry this week. That should allow for some receding of the floodwaters," said Mike Palmerino, agricultural meteorologist at Weather Services Corp.
Most Midwest areas should be dry this week so farmers can prepare fields for planting.
Highs in the 50s and 60s degrees Fahrenheit also were forecast, said Palmerino.
"There will be some work (planting) done, but it will depend on soil temperatures," he said.

Ohio grain merchandisers said 60-degree-and-higher temperatures this past weekend allowed some farmers to plant corn and soybeans. From Indiana to Nebraska, dealers said soil temperatures were too cool for planting, plus weekend rainfall made fields too wet for equipment.

Weather Express Inc meteorologist Fred Gesser said nearly all of the hard red winter wheat area from Kansas to northern Texas should receive at least a 0.25 inch of rain this week, with 0.5 to 1.5 inches likely in central Oklahoma and northern Texas late Tuesday and early Wednesday.
"While all of this is happening (in the Plains) the Corn Belt will be drier and drier," he said.
Weather Services' Palmerino also forecast rain for the central and southern Plains by Wednesday, with more likely Thursday and Friday.
"But, western Kansas is very questionable in terms of getting any significant moisture," he said.
Palmerino said freeze-damaged winter wheat in Kansas and Oklahoma needed moisture to recover and put out new tillers.
